description: Analyse THIS design together with other designs — a dependency, a partner system, a hub's members — and report the problems at the join: what only shows up when they are present together. It imports theirs beside yours and runs reflow2's ORDINARY checks over the whole, so a seam problem arrives as the gap it already is: a contract with no provider, a requirement nothing satisfies across the join. NOTHING IS WRITTEN: the combined graph is built in memory and thrown away, and each design's ids are namespaced, so none overwrites another. ONE other design: `design` (an export, with `namespace`), or `other_graph_id` on a registry server behind a trusted host; findings come back OURS / THEIRS / SEAM. SEVERAL at once, for an effort across a hub's designs: `other_graph_ids`, or `tracked_designs: true` for every design this one pins (through a hub's address, every member). Served alone (the --call door) each is read from its committed export, on a registry from its live store; findings come back `by_design`, `by_pair` ('a×b') and `across`, and each design not read is named in `not_composed`. Run it over a hub before changing what several of its designs share. Where they touch is read from their records on EXACT evidence only (the same file, or a pin naming the other) and drawn as a `computed` link the checks see across; a similar name is only a `candidate` to confirm. ⚠ `link_status` says, per pair: linked, candidates_only, never_touch or not_checked, never that they agree.

budget_chars.description:
How many characters of JSON the reply may spend (default 30,000 when
several designs are composed; unbounded for one other design unless
given). Over it, prose is cut first, then the longest finding lists
are sampled and named in `budget.lists_shortened`; every count stays.

design.description:
The other design, as an export document (what `export_graph` returns).
Pass this OR `other_graph_id`, never both.

namespace.description:
Prefix for the other design's ids — usually its `graph_id`. Required
with `design`: without it the two designs' ids would collide, which is
the entire reason this is not `import_graph`. With `other_graph_id` it
defaults to that graph_id.

other_graph_id.description:
The other design BY GRAPH_ID, on a server that holds many designs (a
registry behind a trusted host): it is read from the design the server
already holds, inside the set of designs the host says you may read.
Refused on a single-design server, and for a design outside that set.

other_graph_ids.description:
SEVERAL designs at once, by graph_id: all are composed with this one
in ONE combined graph, and each finding is attributed to the one
design, the pair of designs or the several designs it names. Served alone
(stdio, the --call door), each must be a design this one pins
(external_dependency with that graph_id), read from its committed
export; on a server holding many designs, from its live store inside
the set the host says you may read. Not with `design`,
`other_graph_id` or `namespace`: each design's ids carry its graph_id.

tracked_designs.description:
`true` composes this design with EVERY design it pins, as
`other_graph_ids` would; each one that could not be read is named in
`not_composed` with a `state` and why. Through a hub's address: every
member of the view.

name: compose_and_analyse
title: Compose and Analyse Designs Together
